newsitem.title: USA: Lili gains strength, headed for Cuba, Florida.
newsitem.headline: Lili gains strength, headed for Cuba, Florida.

text.p: Tropical Storm Lili gained strength Wednesday as it churned through the northwest Caribbean toward Cuba and the Florida Keys, National Hurricane Center said.
At 1100 EDT/1500 GMT, the center of Lili was near latitude 18.6 north and longitude 84.0 west, about 335 miles (535 km) south-southwest of Havana.

Forecasters said the storm appeared to be strengthening and could become a hurricane later Wednesday. It was moving north at about eight mph (13 kph) and had maximum sustained winds near 60 mph (95 kph).

The government of Cuba extended a hurricane watch and issued a tropical storm warning for the Isle of Youth and the western mainland provinces of Matanzas, Villa Clara and Cienfuegos as well as Pinar del Rio and Havana.
A tropical storm warning was in effect along the east coast of Mexico's Yucatan Peninsula from Cabo Catoche southward to Bahia de Chetumal, the hurricane center said.
A tropical storm warning was in effect for the Cayman Islands, and forecasters said a hurricane watch was likely to be issued for the Florida Keys later on Wednesday.
Tropical Storm Lili would become a hurricane if its maximum sustained winds reached 74 mph (119 kph).
